title: Elasticity & Price Discrimination

learningObjectives.text: Know and understand the following concepts: own price elasticity, inelastic and elastic demand, the total revenue test, cross price elasticity
Know how to calculate the various forms of elasticity and understand how they relate to strategy

keyTerms.def: A measure of responsiveness of one variable to changes in another variable; the percentage change in one variable relative to changes in another; a measure of sensitivity (e.g., price-sensitive customers).
OPE = %ΔQx/%ΔPx = (∂Qx/∂Px)(Px/Qx). OPE will always be negative (law of demand).
OPE < −1. Consumers are relatively price sensitive.
−1 < OPE < 0. Consumers are relatively price insensitive.

(1) If demand is elastic (OPE < −1), a price increase (decrease) leads to a decrease (increase) in total revenue. (2) If inelastic (−1 < OPE < 0), a price increase (decrease) leads to an increase (decrease) in total revenue. (3) Total revenue is maximized when demand is unitary elastic.
CPE = %ΔQx/%ΔPy = (∂Qx/∂Py)(Py/Qx). Can be negative or positive: positive → substitutes (Dr Pepper vs. Mr. Pibb); negative → complements (milk and cereal).
%ΔQx/%ΔI; positive for normal goods, negative for inferior goods.

elasticityAndStrategy.Rivalry: CPE between rival brands: high CPE → buyers switch brands easily → intense rivalry
elasticityAndStrategy.Buyer power: OPE of the firm's demand: elastic (OPE < −1) → price-sensitive buyers → strong buyer power
elasticityAndStrategy.Threat of substitutes: CPE with products outside the industry: high CPE → close substitutes → strong threat, caps prices
elasticityAndStrategy.Supplier power / Threat of entry: Not captured by demand elasticity; needs other evidence
elasticityAndStrategy.rule: The larger the elasticity (in absolute value), the stronger the force — and the less pricing power the firm has.

traps: OPE is reported as NEGATIVE; elastic means OPE < −1 (|OPE| > 1)
Use the ORIGINAL (old) price and quantity as the base in the algebraic formula
Use the partial derivative coefficient (∂Q/∂P), not the inverse-demand slope
Netflix: measure the subscriber loss against the expected 25M, not the reported 800K
CPE sign: + substitutes, − complements; magnitude can differ by direction (DP 1.2 vs MP 2.0)
Revenue max at |OPE| = 1, not at maximum quantity
